Lamps and next targets

See how each set compares with its targets. Review what to lift next.

Block Pro

Read the three lamps

White is a pass. Red is a miss. One red lamp makes the set a no lift, and the reason shows on the set screen.

Reps
Passes when you reach the target reps, or the bottom of a rep range.
Load
Passes at the planned load or above. For assisted lifts, the planned assistance or less passes.
Effort
Passes at or under the lift's target RPE, which is 8 unless you set one. No RPE counts as a pass.

When a set is not judged

Warm-ups, drop sets, prep lifts, and sets with no planned load or reps are not judged. Without Pro, you can log the same sets with no lamps.

The estimated-max pass

A weight-and-reps set that beats the target's estimated max passes reps and load together. The calculation is load × (1 + reps / 30). For example, 360 × 8 beats a target of 365 × 6.

The set screen starts effort at the lift's target RPE. Choose another number when the set was easier or harder.

The trainer reads all three sets for the next targets. Until you approve them, the next session starts at the numbers you lifted with Block Pro, or at the workout's numbers without it.

Next targets from the trainer

Block ProiOS 27

After you save a session, the AI trainer reads the loads, reps, effort, notes, rep ranges, and week of the block. It proposes each lift's next targets with a reason.

The trainer can add reps, add load, or hold when it gives a reason. It uses loads your gym can make. A deload week is marked on Today; the trainer proposes lighter numbers for that session only.

The lamps record what happened. They do not change a load by themselves.

Approve each lift

Compare the current and proposed sets. Approve saves a line to the workout. Reject leaves it unchanged. Approve all and Reject all decide the lines that still wait. A hold needs no decision.

Until you approve new targets, a Pro session starts at the numbers last lifted. Without Pro, it starts at the workout's numbers. Starting a session does not save new targets.
